nodes.description: Reduced ATM output weakens the damage-response signal that arrests the cell cycle and licenses repair after a double-strand break. ATM is a damage sensor rather than a repair effector, so the resulting defect is a checkpoint defect and not a collapse of homologous recombination — a distinction that carries directly into how these tumours respond to PARP inhibition.

nodes.description: Female breast cancer at moderately increased risk, enriched for oestrogen-receptor-positive disease rather than the triple-negative pattern seen with some other homologous-recombination genes. Two published estimates of that risk are recorded below and they are not interchangeable, because their designs answer different questions. A population-based case-control study gives an odds ratio of 1.82, with a confidence interval from 1.46 to 2.27, for breast cancer overall, and reports the association as restricted to oestrogen-receptor-positive disease. Family-based segregation analysis in the Australian Breast Cancer Family Registry gives a cumulative risk to age 80 of 13 per cent, with a confidence interval from 4.6 to 30 that reflects both the small number of informative families and heterogeneity among the pathogenic alleles pooled into it. The case-control odds ratio says how much a carrier's risk is multiplied; the segregation analysis says what proportion of carriers develop the disease. Neither is the disease's penetrance, since this is a multi-site predisposition and both figures are specific to female breast cancer.

nodes.description: The dominant-negative route. Selected missense and in-frame deletion alleles make a stable but catalytically dead subunit that enters mixed dimers with the wild-type subunit and blocks its activation. Because Ser1981 autophosphorylation is intermolecular, such a carrier loses considerably more than half of ATM activity, which is why risk is allele-specific rather than uniform across pathogenic carriers.

nodes.description: Radiotherapy is not withheld from a carrier. This is the management statement with the most history behind it, because biallelic ATM loss causes clinical radiosensitivity and that was long assumed to extend to heterozygotes. A population-based contralateral-breast-cancer study found that radiotherapy did not modify the contralateral risk carried by known pathogenic variants, and concluded that altering radiotherapy plans on that basis is unwarranted. The same study found an elevated radiotherapy-associated contralateral risk confined to carriers of rare ATM missense variants of uncertain significance, which is a different group from the pathogenic carriers this entry is about and is a reason the question is not closed rather than a reason to withhold treatment. Note that this coexists with the raised micronucleus formation after irradiation recorded on the Genomic Instability in Glandular Epithelium node, and the two are not in conflict: a measurable difference in a cellular damage assay did not translate into a measurable difference in contralateral breast cancer after radiotherapy in a population-based cohort. The cellular result is why the question was asked; the cohort result is what answers it for management.

nodes.description: Bilateral risk-reducing mastectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, or both may be considered, but neither is routinely recommended on the basis of carrier status alone. The decision is taken against a personalised risk assessment that includes family history, by shared decision-making. This is the practical consequence of the moderate risk tier: the same surgery that is standard advice in a high-penetrance syndrome is optional here.
